_meta.source: Hand-curated. Religion is a short summary of the latest national census or survey and is approximate. Verify before relying on it. English levels are our own estimates (1 = hard, 5 = easy almost everywhere); compare with the EF English Proficiency Index and the EU Eurobarometer language survey.

countries.name: Albania
countries.religion: Mostly Muslim (about half); Catholic and Orthodox minorities; many non-religious or undeclared
notes: Cash is still king outside Tirana and the coast.
Furgons (minibuses) often leave when full rather than on a timetable.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian (~70%); Muslim (~20%) and Catholic minorities
notes: Uses the euro without being in the EU.
Coast is busy and pricier in July–August.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.religion: Muslim (~50%), Orthodox (~30%), Catholic (~15%)
notes: Landmines remain in some rural areas: stay on marked paths when hiking.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian (~80%); small Catholic and Muslim minorities
notes: Serbia does not recognise Kosovo's borders. If you enter Kosovo from Albania, Montenegro or North Macedonia, you may be refused entry when crossing directly from Kosovo into Serbia. Route via North Macedonia or Montenegro instead.

english.script: Cyrillic and Latin (both used on signs)

countries.name: Kosovo
countries.religion: Mostly Muslim (~90%); small Catholic and Orthodox minorities
notes: See the Serbia note about crossing between Kosovo and Serbia.

countries.name: North Macedonia
countries.religion: Orthodox Christian (~45%), Muslim (~30%)

countries.name: Croatia
countries.religion: Mostly Catholic (~80%)
notes: In Schengen since 2023: days here count toward the 90/180 limit.
Dalmatian coast prices peak in July–August.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.religion: Mostly Catholic; large non-religious share

countries.name: Greece
countries.religion: Mostly Greek Orthodox (~90%)
notes: Heatwaves above 40°C are common in July–August.

english.script: Greek alphabet (signs in tourist areas also in Latin script)

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian (~65%); Muslim minority (~10%)
notes: Full Schengen member since 2025: days count toward 90/180.
Adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.
Shaking your head can mean 'yes' and nodding 'no'.

countries.name: Romania
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian (~75%); Catholic and Protestant minorities
notes: Full Schengen member since 2025: days count toward 90/180.

countries.name: Moldova
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian (~90%)
notes: Transnistria is a breakaway region outside government control; check advisories before going.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.religion: Catholic and Reformed Christian; large non-religious and undeclared shares

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.religion: Mostly Catholic (~55%); ~25% non-religious

countries.name: Czechia
countries.religion: Mostly non-religious; small Catholic minority

countries.name: Poland
countries.religion: Mostly Catholic (~70%)
notes: Most shops are closed on Sundays.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.religion: Mostly Catholic (~75%)

countries.name: Latvia
countries.religion: Mixed Lutheran, Catholic and Orthodox; large non-religious share

countries.name: Estonia
countries.religion: Mostly non-religious; Orthodox and Lutheran minorities
notes: Narva is the main land crossing point into Russia (Narva–Ivangorod).

otherLanguages: Russian (widely spoken in Tallinn and Narva)

countries.name: Russia
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian; Muslim minority; many non-religious
notes: Visa/Mastercard cards issued abroad do not work: bring enough cash (EUR/USD).
No direct flights between the EU and Russia; land crossings from the Baltics are limited and change often.
Travel insurance may not cover Russia.

english.script: Cyrillic (Moscow and St Petersburg metro also signed in English)

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian; Greek Catholic minority

countries.name: Belarus
countries.religion: Mostly Orthodox Christian; Catholic minority

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.religion: Mix of Buddhism, Taoism and folk religion; small Christian minority
notes: Typhoon season is July–October, and earthquakes are common.
Plugs and voltage (110V) are like North America.

english.script: Traditional Chinese characters; MRT and main signs also in English

countries.name: Japan
countries.religion: Shinto and Buddhist traditions; most people are not religious in daily life
notes: Tipping is not customary and is often refused.
Some common cold and allergy medicines are banned: check before you pack.
Carry your passport: it is required for tax-free shopping and hotel check-in.

english.script: Japanese (kanji, hiragana, katakana); stations and big-city signs also in English

countries.name: Thailand
countries.religion: Mostly Theravada Buddhist (~93%); Muslim minority in the far south
notes: Laws protecting the monarchy are strict: do not criticise the royal family.
Cover shoulders and knees in temples.

english.script: Thai script; tourist areas also in English

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.religion: Mostly folk religion or not religious; Buddhist and Catholic minorities
notes: Traffic is intense: cross streets slowly and steadily so scooters can flow around you.
Typhoons hit the central coast mostly September–November.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.religion: Islam (official, ~64%); Buddhist, Christian and Hindu minorities
notes: Dress modestly at mosques; alcohol is expensive outside duty-free Langkawi.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.religion: Buddhist (~31%), Christian, Muslim, Taoist and Hindu; ~20% no religion
notes: Rules are strictly enforced: fines for littering, jaywalking and eating or drinking on the MRT.
Drug offences carry very severe penalties.

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.religion: Mostly Theravada Buddhist (~97%)
notes: US dollars are used alongside riel: prices are often in dollars, change in riel.
Cover shoulders and knees at Angkor and other temples.

english.script: Khmer script; tourist areas also in English
